title: Linear functions y = ax + b
summary: Interpret, evaluate and determine linear functions using their rate of change and constant term.
objectives: Interpret a and b in a linear function y = ax + b.
Evaluate a function for a given input and solve for an input from an output.
Determine a linear function from two input-output pairs.

sections.title: Interpret the rate of change and starting value

blocks.text: In y = ax + b, the coefficient a is the change in y for each increase of 1 in x, and b is the output when x = 0. The value b is therefore the y-intercept. Substitute input values using brackets, especially when x or a is negative.

A positive a produces a line that rises from left to right; a negative a produces a line that falls; a = 0 gives a horizontal line. Increasing |a| makes the line steeper when both axes use fixed scales.

sections.title: Evaluate an output or work backwards to an input

blocks.text: To evaluate a function, replace x with the given input and follow the order of operations. To find an input from a known output, replace y and solve the resulting linear equation. Keep the equation balanced at every step.
A common error is to ignore the sign of the substituted value. Writing the substitution line before calculating makes the multiplication of two negative numbers visible.

sections.title: Determine a linear function from values

blocks.text: Given two input-output pairs, first divide the change in output by the matching change in input to find a. Then substitute either complete pair into y = ax + b to find b. Never assume b from the first listed output unless that pair has x = 0.

Verify the finished rule using the other pair. If it fails, recheck the subtraction order and signs. Swapping both subtraction orders leaves the ratio unchanged, but swapping only one reverses the sign incorrectly.

sections.title: Worked example: determine a function from two points

prompt.text: A linear function has y = 6 when x = 1 and y = 15 when x = 4. Find its rule and then find the output when x = -2.

content.text: Find the rate of change from the two pairs.
Write the rule and substitute x = -2.

sections.verification_note: The second original pair checks the rule because 3(4) + 3 = 15; the new output follows from the same constant rate.

sections.title: Worked example: interpret a decreasing function

prompt.text: A container starts with 18 litres and drains at 2.5 litres per minute. Let V be the remaining volume after t minutes. Write V as a function of t, find V after 4 minutes, and find when 3 litres remain.

content.text: The initial value is 18 and the rate is negative because the volume decreases.

sections.verification_note: After 6 minutes the amount drained is 2.5 × 6 = 15 litres, leaving 18 − 15 = 3 litres. The physical domain ends when the container becomes empty.

prompt.text: For y = -2x + 7, find y when x = 4.

blocks.text: Read a as the change in output per unit input and b as the output at x = 0. Substitute with brackets, and solve a linear equation when the output is given instead.
From two pairs, find a using matched changes, then find b from one whole pair. Verify the final function with the unused pair and interpret the sign and domain in context.
